title: C++ I/O and types
outcome: Write C++ programs that read from standard input, write to standard output, and use fundamental data types including int, long long, double, char, and string for basic computation tasks.
rationale: Input/output operations and type systems form the foundation of every competitive programming solution. Without mastery of these, learners cannot read problem constraints, process test data, or produce correctly formatted output.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can read two integers, compute a result, and print the output correctly for Luogu P1001 A+B Problem without consulting references.

title: C++ control flow and functions
outcome: Implement C++ programs using conditional statements including if/else and switch, loops including for and while, and custom functions with parameters and return values to control program execution flow.
rationale: Control flow and functions are the building blocks of algorithmic thinking. Conditionals model decision logic, loops handle repetition, and functions encapsulate reusable computation patterns essential for any non-trivial problem.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can write a function that processes an array with a loop, uses conditionals for branching, and passes all test cases for Luogu P5710 数的性质 without external help.

title: C++ containers
outcome: Select and apply standard C++ containers including vector, string, and array to store, access, and manipulate ordered collections of data in algorithmic problem solving.
rationale: Standard library containers eliminate manual memory management and provide battle-tested data structures. Understanding when to use vector versus array versus string directly determines whether a solution is correct and efficient.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can choose the appropriate container for a problem, iterate over elements with range-based for loops, and solve LeetCode 88 合并两个有序数组 independently.

title: Program decomposition
outcome: Decompose programming problems into smaller reusable functions and modules, applying separation of concerns to build maintainable solutions with clear interfaces and testable components.
rationale: Large problems cannot be solved in a single monolithic block of code. Decomposition into smaller, testable functions reduces cognitive load, enables parallel debugging, and is the prerequisite skill for all advanced algorithm design.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can break down a problem into three or more cooperating functions, define clear parameter contracts, and solve LeetCode 412 Fizz Buzz without looking at solutions.

title: Debugging and testing
outcome: Diagnose and fix common C++ bugs using systematic debugging techniques including breakpoints, print-based tracing, and structured test case construction with boundary analysis.
rationale: Even experienced programmers spend more time debugging than writing code. Systematic debugging with tools and structured test cases transforms frustrating guesswork into a repeatable engineering discipline.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can reproduce a failing test case from output alone, identify the logical error through systematic debugging, and correct it for NowCoder 319811 小红的字符串处理.

title: Git and build workflow
outcome: Initialize Git repositories, stage and commit changes with meaningful messages, and compile C++ programs using command-line build tools in a reproducible development workflow.
rationale: Version control and reproducible builds are non-negotiable professional skills. Git protects against lost work and enables experimentation, while command-line compilation removes IDE dependency for consistent results.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can initialize a Git repository, commit changes with descriptive messages, compile a multi-file C++ program, and explain the build pipeline to another learner.

title: Complexity analysis
outcome: Analyze the time and space complexity of algorithms using Big-O notation, estimate worst-case behavior from nested loops and recursive calls, and justify efficiency trade-offs between competing approaches.
rationale: Algorithm complexity is the universal language for comparing solutions. Without Big-O analysis, learners cannot predict whether their code will run within time limits or choose between competing algorithmic approaches.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can estimate the time complexity of a nested-loop solution to within one order of magnitude, predict whether it passes the standard OJ constraints for LeetCode 217 存在重复元素, and optimize accordingly.

title: Sorting and binary search
outcome: Implement common sorting algorithms and binary search, apply C++ standard library sort and lower_bound functions, and solve problems requiring ordered data access patterns and efficient lookup.
rationale: Sorting and binary search appear in the majority of intermediate competitive programming problems. The C++ standard library provides optimized implementations, but learners must understand when and how to apply them correctly.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can sort an array with std::sort, use lower_bound for binary search, and independently solve LeetCode 704 二分查找 using the two approaches combined.

title: Stacks and queues
outcome: Model and solve problems using stack with LIFO semantics and queue with FIFO semantics, including bracket matching, expression evaluation, and breadth-first traversal preparation tasks.
rationale: Stacks and queues model real-world ordering constraints and appear as building blocks in graph traversal, expression parsing, and state management. Mastering them now prevents re-deriving these patterns during harder graph problems.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can recognize a stack or queue problem from its description, implement the solution with std::stack or std::queue, and solve LeetCode 20 有效的括号 without external references.

title: Hashing and linked structures
outcome: Apply hash-based containers including unordered_map and unordered_set for O(1) average-time lookups and implement linked-list traversal for problems requiring sequential pointer-based access patterns.
rationale: Hash tables provide amortized constant-time lookup that transforms quadratic-time nested loops into linear scans. Linked structures introduce pointer-based traversal, a fundamental pattern for trees and graphs ahead.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can use unordered_map for frequency counting, detect duplicate removal with unordered_set, and solve LeetCode 1 两数之和 using hash-based approaches.

title: Trees, recursion, and traversal
outcome: Represent tree structures in C++, implement recursive and iterative depth-first traversals, and solve problems involving subtree queries, path sums, and ancestor relationships efficiently.
rationale: Trees model hierarchical relationships found in file systems, organization charts, and parse trees. Recursive traversal is the essential mental model for divide-and-conquer algorithms and dynamic programming on trees.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can build a tree from parent or edge input, write a recursive DFS to aggregate subtree values, and solve LeetCode 94 二叉树的中序遍历 without consulting the editorial.

title: Graphs: BFS and DFS
outcome: Model problems as directed and undirected graphs, implement BFS for shortest-path and level-order traversal, and apply DFS for connectivity analysis, cycle detection, and topological exploration.
rationale: Graphs are the most expressive data structure in computer science, modeling networks, dependencies, and state spaces. BFS and DFS together solve connectivity, shortest-path, and reachability problems throughout advanced competitive programming.
stopping_guidance: Stop when you can represent a graph with adjacency lists, run BFS for shortest-path queries on unweighted graphs, and independently solve NowCoder 319371 走迷宫 using BFS traversal.
